key_insight: AI-Donkey combines expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to make LLM-driven many-body perturbation theory workflows more reliable.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce specialist setup effort for predicting excited-state properties and electron–phonon interactions in materials.
method: Benchmark out-of-the-box LLM agents on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow construction.
Combine expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to address cross-stage inconsistencies.
Demonstrate autonomous calculations and post-processing for 1D, 2D, and bulk materials.
evidence_signal: Out-of-the-box agents averaged 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT benchmarks, respectively; with AI-Donkey, all tested agents produced complete, runnable workflows with no observed run-to-run variation.
watch_item: Runnable workflows do not alone establish numerical accuracy; reliability beyond the tested systems and software configurations remains to be assessed.
paper_title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
